edit_summary: Let capture retry matching measure its inner subject length from the wrong base cursor.
root_cause: The capture retry loop starts the inner match at s + j, so the length passed to doh must subtract both the pre-capture offset j and the retry shrink j2.
effect_path: For a capture reached after leading subject bytes, the modified length is too large by j and lets nested alternation or literal matching read past the provided subject slice.
guard_p1: A regex has a capture after at least one literal byte and a following suffix that forces capture retry attempts near the end of the subject.
guard_p2: The neighboring regex starts the capture at subject offset zero, or the subject has enough trailing bytes to cover the overstated length.
expected_crash: out-of-bounds subject read during recursive capture retry
hardness_reason: The bad length is introduced in capture retry bookkeeping and consumed by nested doh/bar recursion, so finding it requires tracking both regex and subject cursors.
naturalness_reason: Cursor-base mixups are natural in recursive regex engines because the pointer and length parameters are carried separately.
explanation: The retry loop shrinks the candidate capture but keeps the same s + j base pointer. Dropping the j subtraction gives nested matching a length that extends beyond the subject slice.
boundary_invariant: the length paired with s + j must not exceed s_len - j, and retry j2 must further reduce it
boundary_case: capture begins at j > 0 and retry reaches the end of the subject slice
neighbor_case: capture begins at j == 0 or the subject has enough trailing bytes for the overstated length
oob_site_expected: nested doh/bar path reads subject bytes beyond s + s_len under the inflated length

edit_summary: Pass the pre-quantifier subject length to the recursive suffix matcher after a quantified atom has advanced j2.
root_cause: After a greedy quantifier consumes bytes into j2, the suffix matcher must receive the subject length remaining from s + j2.
effect_path: A quantified atom near the end of the subject makes j2 greater than j; the recursive suffix bar call sees too-large s_len and later match_op can read beyond the original subject slice.
guard_p1: A regex has a greedy * or + followed by a suffix token, and the quantified atom consumes up to the end of the provided subject slice before the suffix is tried.
guard_p2: The neighboring subject leaves a real suffix byte after the quantified run, so the stale and correct lengths both remain in-bounds.
expected_crash: out-of-bounds subject read in recursive suffix matching
hardness_reason: The cause is length accounting in the quantifier backtracking loop, while the read happens in a nested bar/match_op traversal after several state variables are updated.
naturalness_reason: Using the wrong cursor variable in recursive regex length calculations is a common natural bug in backtracking engines.
explanation: The suffix matcher is called on s + j2 and must be bounded by s_len - j2. Reusing s_len - j lets it inspect bytes already consumed by the quantified atom as if they were still ahead.
boundary_invariant: recursive bar calls must pass a length measured from the same subject pointer they pass
boundary_case: j2 advances beyond j and reaches the end of s before a suffix is attempted
neighbor_case: j2 equals j, or an actual suffix byte remains in the subject slice
oob_site_expected: match_op reads from s + j2 plus an offset allowed only by the stale s_len - j bound

edit_summary: Use the next branch table entry when computing the final alternation arm length.
root_cause: The final alternation arm has no following branch delimiter, so its length must be computed from the enclosing bracket end instead of branches[b->branches + i].
effect_path: For the last arm of a bracket with alternatives, doh indexes one entry past that bracket pair's branch range and uses the stale schlong pointer to form a regex slice for bar.
guard_p1: A regex contains an alternation whose earlier arms fail and whose final arm must be attempted.
guard_p2: A neighboring regex whose first arm matches never reaches the final-arm length calculation.
expected_crash: out-of-bounds branch-table read followed by malformed regex slice traversal
hardness_reason: The off-by-one is hidden in alternation dispatch after setup_branch_points has grouped branches, and the bad pointer is consumed by the recursive matcher rather than at parse time.
naturalness_reason: Using the same branch-table formula for ordinary and final alternation arms is a plausible regex-engine maintenance error.
explanation: The final branch is represented by the enclosing bracket length, not by another branch delimiter. The modified selector makes the last arm look for a nonexistent delimiter entry.
boundary_invariant: when i == b->num_branches, the current arm is the final alternation arm and no branches[b->branches + i] entry exists
boundary_case: all previous alternatives fail and i reaches b->num_branches
neighbor_case: an earlier alternative matches, or b->num_branches is zero
oob_site_expected: info->branches[b->branches + i].schlong read in doh for the final arm

root_cause: The original predicate at slre.c:88 is the semantic boundary for len; weakening it admits a boundary value that the following set_len state machine was written to exclude.

naturalness_reason: Boundary predicates around parser cursors and length-derived state are common off-by-one regression sites.
explanation: The original predicate at slre.c:88 is the semantic boundary for len; weakening it admits a boundary value that the following set_len state machine was written to exclude. When the loop index/cursor reaches the one-past boundary re_len, control continues past the edited guard and reaches line+9: return re[0] == '[' ? set_len(re + 1, re_len - 1) + 1 : op_len(re);; that consumer uses the already-advanced parser/cursor state rather than rechecking the original boundary.

edit_summary: Read the branch table entry before confirming that the grouping scan has not reached the end.
root_cause: setup_branch_points depends on C short-circuit order to avoid reading branches[j] after all branch entries have been assigned to brackets.
effect_path: When the scan reaches j == info->num_branches, the reordered condition reads info->branches[j].bracket_index before the end check; with an exact-capacity branch table this is one past the array.
guard_p1: A regex uses the maximum number of alternation operators and then setup scans brackets after the final branch group.
guard_p2: A neighboring regex with one fewer branch keeps branches[j] inside the fixed array even though it may still read uninitialized slack.
expected_crash: out-of-bounds read of regex_info.branches at the grouping boundary
hardness_reason: The failure depends on the parser-populated branch count, stable sorting, and a later grouping pass, not just on a local array index.
naturalness_reason: Reordering a short-circuit condition during readability cleanup is a realistic C bug in table grouping code.
explanation: The grouping loop must test j against num_branches before looking at the entry. Reversing the operands turns the end sentinel into an addressable table element.
boundary_invariant: info->branches[j] is valid only for j < info->num_branches
boundary_case: regex populates exactly MAX_BRANCHES alternation entries and setup scans after the last group
neighbor_case: regex uses fewer alternation entries, leaving j within the allocated branch array
oob_site_expected: info->branches[j].bracket_index load in setup_branch_points when j == info->num_branches == MAX_BRANCHES

edit_summary: Leave the optional capture-output pointer in regex_info uninitialized while preserving the capture count.
root_cause: slre_match must copy both num_caps and caps into regex_info before recursive matching can publish capture ranges.
effect_path: A regex with a nonempty capture reaches bar, which tests info->caps and writes capture offsets through the uninitialized pointer value after successful nested matching.
guard_p1: The caller requests at least one capture slot and the regex contains a capturing group that matches nonempty input.
guard_p2: The neighboring call passes num_caps == 0 or a regex without captures, so bar never consumes info->caps.
expected_crash: uninitialized capture pointer read and possible invalid capture write
hardness_reason: The missing field initialization is at API setup, while the first read is inside recursive capture handling after regex pre-scan and subject matching.
naturalness_reason: Forgetting one field in a small stack context initializer is a natural optional-output-parameter bug.
explanation: The capture count and capture pointer form one invariant. Keeping num_caps while leaving caps uninitialized makes later capture publication trust a stack garbage pointer.
init_site_expected: slre.c:431 slre_match initializes struct regex_info before calling foo
uninit_storage: stack field info.caps in struct regex_info
skip_init_predicate: the API caller supplies num_caps > 0 and a capture-capable regex
first_read_expected: bar checks info->caps != NULL and writes info->caps[bi - 1] after a capture matches
